title: Surjectivity of spectral closed restriction
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] and let $Z\subseteq X$ be a closed subset such that for every $x\in X$ the intersection $Z\cap\overline{\{x\}}$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] (in particular nonempty). Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of sets on $X$ (a functor from the open subsets of $X$, ordered by inclusion, to sets, satisfying the gluing condition for every open covering), and let $\mathcal F|_Z$ be its inverse image along the inclusion $i:Z\to X$: the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] $\theta:i_p\mathcal F\to\mathcal F|_Z$ of the presheaf $i_p\mathcal F:U\mapsto\varinjlim_{V\supseteq U}\mathcal F(V)$ on $Z$ ($V$ open in $X$, colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of sets over the directed set of such $V$ ordered by reverse inclusion, coprojections $\iota^U_V$), i.e. the construction of [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets. Then the restriction map $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal F|_Z)$, $s\mapsto\theta_Z(\iota^Z_X(s))$ (the component at $X$ of the unit $\mathcal F\to i_*(\mathcal F|_Z)$), is surjective.

proof.text: Construct the inverse-image stalk comparison as Presheaf.stalkPullbackHom followed by the stalk map of toSheafify. Both are isomorphisms. The germ compatibility lemmas identify this comparison with the adjunction unit for the explicit sheafification pullback. The canonical left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism transfers bijectivity of the explicit unit to the chosen pullback unit.

proof.text: Prove a private germ-and-gluing criterion for set-valued sheaves F on X, G on Z, and a morphism F to i_*G inducing compatible stalk bijections on Z. Every point specializes to Z by the nonemptiness clause of the connectedness hypothesis. Equality along Z gives equality of germs everywhere and hence injectivity. For a section t of G, stalk surjectivity and local equality of germs give representatives on compact ambient opens; compactness of closed Z gives a finite family U_i, sigma_i covering Z.

proof.text: Let Agree(i,j,y) mean that sigma_i and sigma_j are defined and have equal germs at y. This is open and stable under generalization. The sections agree at points of Z where both are defined. Fix y; connectedness of closure{y} intersect Z implies that any representatives defined near two specializations of y in Z agree at y: partition their finite covering into the unions of the U_i whose germs agree with a chosen one at y and those whose germs do not. A point in the intersection of these two unions contradicts germ transitivity and generalization stability.

proof.text: Put K_i=U_i intersect Z and B_i=U_i intersect union_j(generalizationHull(K_j) minus Agree(i,j)). The K_i are compact, their generalization hulls are closed in the constructible topology, compact opens are closed there, and the complement of the open Agree locus is closed there. Thus B_i is constructibly closed. The proved source-library theorem exists_specializes_of_isClosed_constructibleTopology_of_mem_closure shows that a point specializing into K_i cannot lie in closure(B_i), by the connectedness argument of the preceding step. The opens W_i=U_i minus closure(B_i) therefore cover X. At a point in W_i intersect W_j choose a specialization in some K_k; exclusion from B_i and B_j gives agreement with sigma_k, hence agreement of sigma_i and sigma_j. Apply Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing' and Presheaf.section_ext to glue, and check the image equals t on germs along Z.

proof.text: Apply this fully proved private criterion to the explicit inverse-image unit and the stalk comparisons from the first step, then cancel the left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism and take the surjectivity component. All arguments work for sheaves of sets and use only connectedness of closures of single points, including the forced empty ambient space when Z is empty.

lean.statement:
theorem spectral_closed_restriction_surjective
    (X : TopCat.{u}) [SpectralSpace X]
    (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (hconn : ∀ x : X, ConnectedSpace (↥(Z ∩ closure ({x} : Set X))))
    (F : X.Sheaf (Type u)) :
    let i : TopCat.of Z ⟶ X := TopCat.ofHom ⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩
    let R := (Sheaf.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction (Type u) i).unit.app F
    Function.Surjective
      (fun s : F.1.obj (op ⊤) =>
        (R.1.app (op ⊤)) s)
